subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a detailed armoured hauler truck model: a front cab, armoured chassis, six wheels, a sealed glowing cargo pod, turret, neon strips, light bar, antenna, and SVG decal textures like hazard stripes and logos, aiming for a rich but efficient static model.

I'm figuring out dimensions and placement for the cab, pod, wheels, and chassis, and sketching helper functions for boxes and cylinders to build the geometry. I'm also planning the material kits and textures—panelled metal, glow effects, hazard stripes, warning labels, and decals—plus setting ground-level wheel positioning before diving into actual color definitions.

Working out cab geometry...

Working out the windshield as a thin rotated box angled to match the slope between the hood and roof points, calculating its length and rotation angle so the glass surface aligns with the slanted cab line.

Still placing windshield and side window geometry...

Now I'm adding front details: a bumper with hazard striping, glowing headlights on the hood face, a dark grill with horizontal glow slits, and a roof-mounted light bar with red/blue segments. I'm also placing thin antenna cylinders and twin exhaust stacks behind the cab, then adding armor elements like slanted side skirts over the wheels and angled plating on the cab sides.

Now I'm designing a rear turret on the cab roof with a ring base, turret box, and dual forward-facing barrels with glowing muzzle tips, plus working out the flatbed cargo platform dimensions and a swept ellipse-profile pod to sit on it.

Writing pod sweep geometry...

I'll flat-cap the rear at z=-4.12 with an emblem door facing outward, skipping the front since it joins the cab. For the ring bands, I'm setting up an octagonal lathe sweep (8 segments around the z-axis) forming an annulus shape, rotated 22.5° so vertices align with the pod's top.

Adding glowing cyan accent rings alongside the dark steel straps...

I'm checking the pod taper against the platform width, keeping radius mostly constant at 1.25 except near the rear, and verifying the pod sits properly on the platform with vertices oriented correctly for the ngon sweep.

Now I'm figuring out where to place side details like glowing seals, vent boxes, and "SEALED/BIO-CARGO" labels on the pod's octagonal cross-section, working out the exact vertex angles so flat label panels align with the pod's side faces.

Still working out the octagon geometry...

Checking the panel height against the face span works out fine, so I'll set the lathe ring radii to keep its flat faces and vertices clear of the pod's geometry, settling on an outer radius around 1.5 with the ring outline starting near x=1.2.

Now I'm adding the glow rings with slightly offset radii to match up against the strap edges, then building out the pod's top ridge with a glowing seal-line and vent boxes, plus side panel details like a warning label, status screen, rear emblem, and front coupling, and finally working on the platform's rails, tie-downs, and cradle saddles.

I'm skipping the fuel tanks and instead adding angled armour skirt panels along the platform edges, then placing the four axle positions with appropriately spaced tires and adding rear bumper and tail light details.

Now I'm adding mudguards over the wheel arches, checking that they clear the platform width, and verifying the front cab wheels don't improperly overlap the cab body geometry.

Setting wheel hubs at x=±1.88 with glowing rings, and placing the cab origin at y=1.45 so I can derive the windshield, side window, hood, headlight, and roof heights from there. I'm also working out the extrusion direction so the outline thickness stays centered correctly, then deciding on hull paint color.

For the hull I'm going with a dark gunmetal cyberpunk palette with magenta/cyan accents, using a panelled material with countershading (lighter top, darker bottom, grime overlay) and calculating texel density so seams blur appropriately at the painted surface's scale.

I'm writing a custom "plating" paint function that computes UV coordinates from the dominant surface normal and draws seam lines of a given width at a grid spacing, then planning the texture list — visor, hazard stripes, emblem, side labels — needed for the model.

I'm settling on a decal helper that places a textured plane at a given position and direction, orienting it so the plane faces outward with world-up alignment, so I can apply logos and panel graphics consistently across different mesh faces.

Beyond that I'm layering on extra details: a roof sensor dome, antennas, exhaust stacks, a turret, a front ram, mirror cameras, and a magenta underglow strip along the chassis. I'm also adding bumper spikes made from cones, rear tow hooks, and wheel hubs built from cylinders with a glow ring and small bolt-like boxes, aiming to keep the part count manageable around eight pieces per wheel.

Now I'm defining helper functions to simplify building boxes and other geometry parts, plus setting up a hazard-stripe pattern (diagonal yellow/black) for bumper and skirt decals, and planning the wheel rim's outer glow ring and hub detail before writing out the full construction code.

Still placing cab door plates and windows...

Working out hood vent geometry...

Now I'm designing the front face: a dark grille box with cyan glowing slits, two headlight boxes placed symmetrically with a white-cyan glow, and figuring out bumper placement relative to the front axle position.

Positioning the bumper between the chassis and cab, overlapping slightly with the front face, with a hazard decal plane mounted on its front surface. I'm also sketching ram-wedge spikes or cones on top of the bumper for an aggressive look.

Now I'm laying out the roof: an armor box panel above the cab, a front-mounted light bar made of alternating magenta/cyan glowing segments, and a ring-shaped turret base positioned further back on the roof.

Now I'm adding exhaust stacks behind the cab with glowing orange caps, thin antenna rods on the roof with red glowing tips, and mirror arms with glowing cyan camera boxes near the windshield.

For the chassis, I'm defining the dark frame beam running the length of the vehicle, adding magenta glowing underglow strips along the sides, and setting up the axles, tires, hubs, and glow rings for the wheels.

Now I'm working out the wheel outer face positions, adding thin cyan glow rings and dark center caps, then moving to mudguards sized and positioned over the rear axles, considering whether they'd intersect the cab at the front.

Next I'm placing the flatbed platform, matching its height to meet the chassis and cab bottom, checking its width and length against the frame rails and rear position.

Now I'm adding side rails with hazard stripe decals, planning to tile several smaller planes with correct aspect ratio so the stripe texture doesn't stretch distortedly, then positioning saddle supports under the pod at the ring mount points.

Skipping the saddles since the gap between pod bottom and platform top is negligible, I'm instead defining the pod as a lathe/sweep shape along a polyline path with constant radius and flat-faced sides, then placing mounting rings at several z-positions along that path using an outline profile.

The glow offset from the strap works out fine at about 0.03 difference. Now I'm designing the pod's rear door as an octagonal armored plate with an emblem panel mounted slightly behind it, checking that the door radius sits inside the pod's flat face dimension.

Adding door handles and a glowing magenta seal ring around the door...

Now I'm placing the pod's top ridge strip and vent boxes, checking their positions against the strap rings to avoid overlap.

I'm also figuring out placement for side panel labels and glowing status screens, slotting them between the straps at different z positions along the pod's body.

Writing pod paint shader...

Still writing plating function...

Now I'm sketching the SVG textures for the cyberpunk palette: a visor with dark gradient background, cyan HUD lines, a magenta triangle, and "CONVOY 07" text; a smaller sidewinder glass with diagonal cyan glints; and a hazard stripe texture with yellow rectangles and black triangles.

I'm also designing an "AEGIS" door logo with a shield outline and subdued glow, a yellow cargo label with "SEALED CARGO" and "CLASS-9" text plus barcode marks, and a screen texture with dark background and green/cyan graph bars.

Now I'm adding a round biohazard-style seal emblem with a magenta ring and glow, a rear plate reading "NX-4471," and glowing red tail light boxes near the rear bumper, bringing the total texture count to eight. For the cab-to-pod coupling, I'm placing connector cylinders and hose geometry with glowing rings to bridge the gap between the two sections.

Now I'm adding sweeping hose connectors between the cab and pod using catmull curves, plus a yellow cable, then calculating skirt armor plate positions along the chassis—placed midway between the axles—accounting for the narrow wheel gaps that limit plate length.

Skipping the roof blades idea, I'll add a brush guard instead: two angled rods running from the hood front forward to the bumper with a crossbar, using thin rounded-end rods.

Tires get a dark tread color with hub detailing, and I'm defining a cylinder helper function for quick part creation with optional direction. Checking that overall dimensions stay sensible — antenna topping out under 5 units tall, body length spanning roughly 9.6 units front to back.

Writing a texture-plane helper for hazard strip decals, then assembling the full build with wheel centers set so tires sit flush on the ground.
